match.reason: No existing point teaches ecologically sustainable development; the closest ones, costs of growth and macroeconomic objectives, only touch on pollution or wider aims and do not teach the idea of meeting today's needs without harming future generations.

draft.title: Ecologically sustainable development
card: Ecologically sustainable development (ESD) is economic growth that meets the needs of people today without harming the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
It treats the environment as a stock of resources that can be used up or damaged. Using it faster than it can renew itself leaves less for later.
ESD asks decision makers to weigh economic, social and environmental effects together, rather than looking at output and income alone.
A fishing industry that takes only as many fish as the population can replace each year can keep going. One that takes more each year may run the stock down.
draft.remember: ESD means meeting today's needs while leaving future generations able to meet theirs.

a.q: Which action best fits the aim of ecologically sustainable development?
opts: Harvesting a forest at a rate that allows it to regrow
Clearing a forest quickly to raise this year's output
Leaving a forest untouched so no one can ever use it
Harvesting a forest and leaving regrowth to future councils
a.why: Harvesting at a rate the forest can renew meets today's needs and leaves resources for the future. Clearing it quickly raises output now but reduces what future generations can use. Leaving it untouched ignores the needs of people today.
a.clue: Look for the option that serves both present and future people.

b.q: A town in Queensland has a groundwater supply that refills slowly. Farmers pump out more each year than flows back in, and farm incomes are rising. Why does this not fit ESD?
opts: It lowers the water future generations can use
It raises farm incomes, which ESD aims to limit
It uses water, and ESD allows no use of resources
It benefits farmers only, and not the wider town
b.why: Pumping out more than refills the supply means less water is left for future users, even though incomes rise now. ESD does not ban resource use or growth. It asks that use does not harm future needs.
b.clue: Compare how fast water is taken with how fast it is replaced.

a.best: Harvesting a forest at a rate that allows it to regrow

b.best: It lowers the water future generations can use

problems.detail: The option 'Harvesting a forest and leaving regrowth to future councils' is unclear. It could mean the forest regrows for the future, or that the job of replanting is handed to later councils. The why for (a) does not explain why this option is wrong, so a student who picks it gets no guidance.

opts: Harvesting a forest at a rate that allows it to regrow
